plan.summary: Two-show review columns carried one score/pull quote onto both shows. Give each show a score and quote from its own section: Bloomberg Gerard (Born Yesterday vs House of Blue Leaves), Theatrely The Pass (pull quote was Hungry Women's). Interested Bystander (bug/two-strangers) already split into per-show sections, 74/74 is coincidence, no change.
steps: The Pass: humanReviewScore 74 + own pull quote

actions.oldValue: So go for Kanin’s savvy script and for one truly inspired comic performance.
actions.newValue: But it’s Edie Falco who will steal your heart as Bananas, a depressive who fries up Brillo pads for hamburgers
actions.description: Pull quote was copied from the Born Yesterday half of the Bloomberg column

actions.newValue: BRO-4594: Bloomberg column reviews two shows. Born Yesterday section is rated **1/2 of 4 (Arianda raved, Belushi brutish, Leonard pallid); the 78 came from scoring the whole column including the Leaves praise. Scored on this section only.

actions.description: Born Yesterday section is **1/2, not the 3-star Leaves rating

actions.newValue: BRO-4594: Theatrely column covers The Pass and Hungry Women. The Pass section is positive (magnetic lead, strong staging) with reservations (genre feels passe, over-compensatory bro-isms). Pull quote was from the Hungry Women section. Scored on The Pass section only.

actions.oldValue: Daniella Caggiano’s production remains engaging and highly enjoyable.
actions.newValue: It’s a magnetic performance well-suited to Max Hunter’s staging, which opts for exclamation points over question marks and successfully brings the play into 2026.
actions.description: Pull quote was about Hungry Women
